title: In the interim path an Agent's own Artifact edits require a Ranked Delegate trigger and survive Core Facilitator misalignment review
content:
A.2.2.6.2.3.2 routes Prime Agents without an operational Root Edit Primitive through Core GovOps and the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle, on a fixed clock: the Agent submits a draft by 23:59 UTC Monday (A.2.2.6.2.3.2.1), Core GovOps drafts the formal proposal, shares it back, and submits it for the following Monday's vote (A.2.2.6.2.3.2.2).

Two gates then sit above the Agent. A.2.2.6.2.3.2.3: the proposal is decided by SKY holders only "if triggered by a Ranked Delegate and not rejected by the Core Facilitator for misalignment," and "A proposal that is not triggered or is rejected by the Core Facilitator for misalignment is treated as rejected." Inaction is therefore a denial — an Agent's edit fails silently if no Ranked Delegate picks it up.

A third gate is discretionary. A.2.2.6.2.3.2.2.1 lets Core GovOps delay submission based on the size of the edit, ambiguities, broader issues requiring consultation, the Agent's own responsiveness, and — explicitly — "the overall workload of Core GovOps." An Agent's ability to change itself is thus partly a function of an unrelated party's capacity.

This stands in tension with the design the Atlas describes elsewhere, where a Prime Agent's Artifact "can only be edited through a token holder vote" (A.2.2.1.1.15). Under the interim regime, Agent token holders do not decide; SKY holders do, and only if a Ranked Delegate and Core GovOps both let the question reach them. The counterweight is that once approved, the Agent "may begin operationalizing that logic immediately thereafter" (A.2.2.6.2.3.2.4).
description: Untriggered or misalignment-rejected proposals count as rejected, and Core GovOps may delay submission at discretion — including for its own workload.
